\begin{definition}[Uniform matrix]
\lean{Expander.unifMatrix}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p097-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p098-b003
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p030-b001}
\label{Expander.unifMatrix}
\leanok
For $n$ indices, the uniform matrix is the real matrix whose every entry equals $1/n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Operator norm bound for a stochastic matrix]
\lean{Expander.opNorm_le_one}
\label{Expander.opNorm_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.norm_toCLM_apply_le, Expander.toCLM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with nonnegative entries and every row
sum equal to $1$. The operator norm of the linear map $v\mapsto Av$ on Euclidean space
is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Contractive Matrix Decomposition]
\lean{Expander.exists_decomposition}
\label{Expander.exists_decomposition}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.inner_eq_sum, Expander.inner_toCLM_right, Expander.inner_uniform_self, Expander.lambda, Expander.mulVec_uniform, Expander.norm_mulVec_le_lambda, Expander.toCLM, Expander.toCLM_apply_coord, Expander.toCLM_smul, Expander.toCLM_sub, Expander.unifMatrix, Expander.uniform, Expander.uniform_apply}
\difficulty{7}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $A$ be a symmetric real $n\times n$ matrix with
nonnegative entries and every row summing to $1$. Let $\lambda(A)$ be the supremum of
$\|Av\|$ over unit vectors $v$ orthogonal to the constant vector with every coordinate
$1/n$, and suppose $\lambda(A)\leq \lambda$ for some $\lambda\geq 0$. Then there is a
real $n\times n$ matrix $C$ such that $A=(1-\lambda)J+\lambda C$, where every entry of
$J$ is $1/n$, and the Euclidean operator norm of $C$ is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[One-step transition distribution]
\lean{Expander.stepPMF}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p039-b002,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p039-b003
}
\statementsource{Gil98}{pdf-d5b902970e61-p004-b005}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p021-b002}
\label{Expander.stepPMF}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic}
Given a symmetric stochastic real matrix $A$ on $n$ indices and a starting index $i$,
the one-step distribution assigns probability $A_{ij}$ to each index $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restriction of matrix rows]
\lean{Expander.resMatrix}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p099-b003}
\label{Expander.resMatrix}
\leanok
For a real matrix $A$ indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a subset $B$ of those indices,
the restricted matrix has entry $A_{ij}$ when its row index $i$ belongs to $B$, and
entry $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Entries of a row-restricted matrix]
\lean{Expander.resMatrix_apply}
\label{Expander.resMatrix_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.resMatrix}
\difficulty{1}
For a real matrix $A$ indexed by $	ext{Fin}(n)$ and a subset $B$ of its indices, the
entry in row $i$ and column $j$ of the matrix obtained by retaining only rows indexed by
$B$ is $A_{ij}$ when $i\in B$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restricted matrix iteration]
\lean{Expander.resVec}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p099-b003,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p099-b004
}
\label{Expander.resVec}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.resMatrix, Expander.toCLM}
For a real matrix $A$ indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a subset $B$ of those indices,
define a sequence of vectors in $\mathbb R^n$ as follows: the initial vector has
coordinate $1/n$ on $B$ and $0$ outside $B$. Each subsequent vector is obtained by
applying the linear map associated with the matrix whose rows outside $B$ are zero and
whose rows in $B$ agree with $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the restricted iterates]
\lean{Expander.resVec_nonneg}
\label{Expander.resVec_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.resVec}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on $	ext{Fin}(n)$, meaning that it is
symmetric, has nonnegative entries, and each row sums to $1$. For every finite subset
$B$ of $	ext{Fin}(n)$, every integer $k\ge 0$, and every index $j$, the $j$th coordinate
of the $k$th restricted iterate is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate sum bounded by the Euclidean norm]
\lean{Expander.sum_le_sqrt_mul_norm}
\label{Expander.sum_le_sqrt_mul_norm}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every vector $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with the Euclidean norm, its coordinate sum
satisfies $\sum_{j=1}^n x_j\le \sqrt{n}\,\|x\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial restricted-vector norm bound]
\lean{Expander.norm_resVec_zero_le}
\label{Expander.norm_resVec_zero_le}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.resVec}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $A$ be any real $n\times n$ matrix, and let
$B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ have size at most $\beta n$, where $\beta\ge0$. Define $r_0$
to have entry $1/n$ on $B$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then $\|r_0\|\le\sqrt{\beta}/\sqrt{n}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Norm bound for a restricted matrix]
\lean{Expander.norm_toCLM_resMatrix_le}
\label{Expander.norm_toCLM_resMatrix_le}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.exists_decomposition, Expander.lambda, Expander.resMatrix, Expander.resMatrix_apply, Expander.toCLM, Expander.toCLM_add, Expander.toCLM_apply_coord, Expander.toCLM_smul, Expander.unifMatrix}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with
nonnegative entries and row sums equal to $1$. Define $\lambda(A)$ as the supremum of
$\|Av\|$ over unit vectors orthogonal to the constant vector whose entries are $1/n$.
Suppose $\lambda(A)\le\lambda$, $0\le\lambda\le1$, and $\beta\ge0$. For a subset
$B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|B|\le\beta n$, let $A_B$ be obtained by replacing the
rows of $A$ outside $B$ by zero. Then every vector $x\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfies
$\|A_Bx\|\le\big((1-\lambda)\sqrt{\beta}+\lambda\big)\|x\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restricted-vector norm bound]
\lean{Expander.norm_resVec_le}
\label{Expander.norm_resVec_le}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.lambda, Expander.norm_toCLM_resMatrix_le, Expander.resMatrix, Expander.resVec, Expander.toCLM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with
nonnegative entries and row sums equal to $1$. Define $\lambda(A)$ as the supremum of
$\|Av\|$ over unit vectors orthogonal to the constant vector with entries $1/n$. Suppose
$\lambda(A)\le\lambda$, $0\le\lambda\le1$, and $\beta\ge0$. For a subset
$B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|B|\le\beta n$, define $r_0$ to have entry $1/n$ on $B$
and $0$ elsewhere, and recursively set $r_{k+1}=A_Br_k$, where $A_B$ is obtained from
$A$ by replacing rows outside $B$ by zero. Then for every integer $k\ge0$,
$\|r_k\|\le\big((1-\lambda)\sqrt{\beta}+\lambda\big)^k\|r_0\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Random walk path distribution]
\lean{Expander.walkPMF}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p099-b003,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p099-b004
}
\statementsource{Gil98}{
  pdf-d5b902970e61-p004-b005,
  pdf-d5b902970e61-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p021-b002,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p029-b002
}
\label{Expander.walkPMF}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.stepPMF}
Given a symmetric stochastic real matrix $A$ on $n$ indices, where $n$ is positive, the
distribution on paths of length $k$ starts with a uniformly chosen index and then, at
each step, chooses the next index according to the row of $A$ corresponding to the
current index.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of an initial walk]
\lean{Expander.walkPMF_zero_apply}
\label{Expander.walkPMF_zero_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.walkPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space, and define
the walk process by choosing its initial state uniformly. Every walk consisting of a
single state has probability $1/n$, where $n$ is the number of states.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of an extended walk]
\lean{Expander.walkPMF_succ_apply}
\label{Expander.walkPMF_succ_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.stepPMF, Expander.walkPMF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space, and let the
probability of a walk of length $k$ be defined by choosing its initial state uniformly
and then taking transitions according to $A$. For every walk $g$ of length $k$ and state
$j$, the probability of the walk obtained by appending $j$ is the probability of $g$
multiplied by the transition probability from its final state to $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint distribution for restricted walks]
\lean{Expander.walk_filter_sum}
\label{Expander.walk_filter_sum}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.resVec, Expander.resVec_nonneg, Expander.walkPMF, Expander.walkPMF_succ_apply, Expander.walkPMF_zero_apply}
\difficulty{7}
Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space, and let $B$
be a set of states. For every $k\in\mathbb N$ and state $j$, the sum of the
probabilities of all walks of length $k$ whose states all lie in $B$ and whose final
state is $j$ equals the $j$th coordinate of the vector obtained by starting with mass
$1/n$ on each state in $B$ and applying the matrix that retains only rows indexed by
$B$, at each of the $k$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on walks contained in a set]
\lean{Expander.walk_all_mem_le}
\label{Expander.walk_all_mem_le}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.lambda, Expander.norm_resVec_le, Expander.norm_resVec_zero_le, Expander.resVec, Expander.resVec_nonneg, Expander.sum_le_sqrt_mul_norm, Expander.walkPMF, Expander.walk_filter_sum}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space of size $n$,
and let $\lambda(A)$ denote its operator norm on vectors orthogonal to the uniform vector.
Suppose this quantity is at most $\lambda$, with $0\leq\lambda\leq1$. If $B$ is a set of
states and $0\leq\beta$ satisfies $|B|\leq\beta n$, then for every $k\in\mathbb N$, the
probability that all states of a length-$k$ walk lie in $B$ is at most
$\bigl((1-\lambda)\sqrt{\beta}+\lambda\bigr)^k$.
\end{theorem}
